slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Exod 15:2: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.
slides.body: “The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.”
slides.heading: Exod 15:2

slides.alt_text: Slide 1: The proposed salvation-name and exaltation connections.
slides.body: Exodus says the LORD became Israel's 'salvation'. Jesus's Hebrew name shares that word's root. Stephen later sees Jesus at God's right hand.
slides.heading: A name hidden in a song?

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Christian salvation theology connects the passages.
slides.body: Matthew explains Jesus's name through his saving mission. Christians can see God's rescue at the sea as a pattern of the salvation they see in Jesus.
slides.heading: The strongest connection

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: The lexical and contextual limits.
slides.body: Exodus uses a common noun: 'salvation', not the name Yeshua. Israel exalts God in praise; that is not Stephen's right-hand scene. The song celebrates rescue already accomplished.
slides.heading: But the Hebrew matters
